newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe farmers deliver 845,000 tonnes of maize.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe farmers deliver 845,000 tonnes of maize.

text.p: Zimbabwean commercial farmers have so far delivered over 845,000 tonnes of maize to the state-owned Grain Marketing Board (GMB) from their last harvest, an industry official said on Wednesday.
GMB board chairman Kumbirayi Katsande said 500,000 tonnes of of the grain was set aside as strategic reserves for the drought-prone southern African country.
Katsande told reporters his board still expected to buy a total of one million tonnes of maize, with the bulk expected to come from small farms.
"Some 58 percent of the maize intake to date has been from the small-farm sector, 41 percent from the large scale farming area and one percent from the Agricultural Development Authority," he said.

Zimbabwe's maize crop is estimated at over two million tonnes following good rains, against 800,000 tonnes produced in the previous drought-hit season. --Stella Mapenzauswa, Harare Newsroom: +263-4 72 52 28/9
